messages:
Maya R.: Quick heads-up — we're at 10% canary for realtimev3 prefetch toggles. If latency spikes or error rate jumps, who is allowed to shut this off immediately? Need to update the runbook with explicit owners and the audit steps.
Sam K.: Eng-infra owns the primary shutdown path. Anyone on eng-infra on-call or the oncall lead can flip in an emergency. Two mandatory things: auth (who flipped) and an audit entry (ticket or comment).
Leo P.: +1. Suggested minimal sequence: 1) notify @eng-oncall and @eng-sre, 2) disable the flag in the feature flag service, 3) verify traffic normalizes (p50/p95), 4) create a rollback tag + incident ticket. Keep it short and observable.
Tara S.: Putting the exact CLI snippet here so it's copy-pasteable for the runbook:
```
# disable prefetch for realtimev3
flagctl set --flag=service.realtimev3.prefetch --value=false --actor="<yourname>" --reason="emergency shutdown RF-<jira>"

# create audit entry (FlagAudit service)
curl -X POST https://flags.internal.audit/record -H 'Authorization: Bearer $AUDIT_TOKEN' -d '{"flag":"service.realtimev3.prefetch","action":"disable","by":"<yourname>","note":"RF-1234 latency spike"}'
```
eng-oncall-bot: guardrail notice — automatic fallback will trigger if p50 latency > 300ms for 5m. Manual flip still allowed; please include the guardrail logs in the ticket. :triangular_flag_on_post:
ops-bot: reminder: always attach a JIRA or incident number when you flip. For customer-impacting rollouts also CC the account manager and @product_lead.
Maya R.: Clarifying question — should the flipper also ping @security? We want audit + post-action review but not alarm product for minor rollbacks.
Sam K.: Ping @security for any suspicious patterns or data-exposure concerns. For normal perf rollbacks, just @eng-oncall + ops-bot + the RFC/JIRA. For Dedicated / private installs follow the SLA playbook and page account ops.
Leo P.: I'll add a small matrix to the runbook listing: who can flip (roles), when to page security, required audit fields (actor, reason, jira), and default TTL (30m) after a flip — then owner must confirm either re-enable or extend.
Maya R.: Perfect. I'll open a PR to the ops-runbook and include the snippets above. Can someone from eng-oncall review before I merge? cc @Sam K. @Leo P.
Sam K.: I'll review within the hour. If you merge, please follow the checklist in the PR description so it's easy to revert.
Tara S.: One more quick guardrail suggestion — require the flipper to run the quick health check after flip: `healthcheck --env=prod --service=realtimev3 --metrics=p50,p95,err_rate`. Add that to the snippet.
Maya R.: Will do. Thanks all. I'll post the finalized runbook link here when PR is merged.
